title: perf(node/udp): shard session map + throttle tracker touch
body:
消除 UDP 热路径上的逐包锁热点(codex 指出的 ①②),并按后续高强度审计做了更深的修法。含两个提交,建议 squash 合并。

## 最终代码做了什么

### 会话表分片(每监听器)
每监听器的 UDP 会话表由 `Mutex<HashMap>` 改为 **DashMap**(按客户端地址分片)。逐包查会话只取分片同步锁(await 前释放),不同客户端的包不再互相串行。新会话走 entry API + 双检竞态。

### tracker 也分片(进程级锁彻底消除)
`ConnectionTracker` 的 UDP 会话表(按 client+rule 键)同样由**进程级 `Mutex<HashMap>` 改为 DashMap**。`udp_touch`/`udp_close` 只取目标分片的锁——连新会话开启/关闭都不再打全局锁。

> 注:最初版本是用"每 15s 最多 touch 一次"的节流来回避进程级锁;审计后改为直接把 tracker 分片,于是**节流逻辑整个删除**(`last_touch` 字段、间隔常量、两处重复代码都没了),恢复"每包双向无条件 touch",代码更简单且连接数计数更准。

## 审计修复(#1–#4)
- **#1** sweeper 与 tracker prune 用 `saturating_sub`:DashMap `len()` 跨分片读取无全局锁,并发插入落在两次读之间不能让 usize 下溢(原本 debug 构建会 panic 杀死清理任务→socket 泄漏;release 出垃圾日志)。
- **#2** 会话中途被清后仍持续计数:改回每包无条件 touch,不再少计。
- **#3** tracker 进程级锁:已分片消除。
- **#4** 重复的节流逻辑:随节流删除而消失。

## 不做(③,单独评估)
入口仍是单 `recv→send` 循环。不限速场景 send 极少真阻塞,真正成本是上面这些锁(已消除);拆分收发需有界队列/背压/保序设计,应等实际 UDP 压测确认瓶颈后再做。

## 验证
新增 `dashmap` 依赖;`cargo clippy -p relay-node` 0 警告;node 测试 84+4 全过;fmt 干净。

title: perf: Prune function bodies from source before building AST
body: We use a Rust/Ruff-based lexer to prune function bodies in cases where we're sure we won't visit them. This makes `compile()` much faster since it has much less code to parse and compile into an AST. Line numbers are kept correct by adding blank lines before a final `pass`. See https://github.com/pawamoy/prune-source/.

title: perf: cache parsed CRL as a compact revocation index
body: # perf: cache parsed CRL as a compact revocation index ## Что изменено При `POST /xml/verify` с проверкой через CRL каждый запрос повторно разбирал все CRL-файлы. Основной GOST CRL размером около 19 МБ: - разбирался заново на каждом запросе; - занимал около 218 МБ в виде `X509CRL`; - создавал основную задержку при проверке подписи. Теперь `CrlService` один раз строит для каждой версии CRL компактный `CrlWrapper` — индекс: ```text издатель → отсортированные серийные номера + дата и причина отзыва ``` Последующие проверки выполняются бинарным поиском без повторного разбора DER. Размер индекса — около 34 МБ вместо 218 МБ. ## Инвалидация кэша Версия файла определяется по: - каталогу; - имени; - времени изменения; - размеру. При удалении или успешной перезаписи CRL индекс дополнительно инвалидируется явно. Индексы удалённых и устаревших файлов очищаются. ## Совместимость Поведение `X509CRL` сохранено: - поиск по издателю и серийному номеру; - поддержка `certificateIssuer` для indirect CRL; - сохранение даты и причины отзыва; - при повторяющейся паре «издатель + серийный номер» используется прежний путь через `X509CRL`, чтобы не менять результат в неоднозначном случае. API и формат ответа не изменялись. ## Результаты A/B-теста ```text Старая версия: 2.048, 1.912, 1.531, 1.500, 1.554 с Новая версия: 2.980, 0.080, 0.066, 0.061, 0.077 с ``` Первый запрос новой версии строит индекс, поэтому занимает около 3 секунд. Последующие запросы используют готовый индекс. Медиана прогретых запросов: ```text 1.55 с → 0.071 с ``` Ускорение — примерно в 22 раза. Обе версии вернули одинаковый результат: подпись валидна, сертификат не отозван. ## Проверка - Полный `./gradlew test` проходит. - Добавлены тесты на: - эквивалентность результатов `X509CRL`; - повторное использование индекса; - замену и удаление CRL; - явную инвалидизацию после перезаписи; - indirect CRL через `certificateIssuer`; - fallback при дублирующихся записях. Изменение локализовано в `CrlService` и новом `CrlWrapper`; внешнее поведение сервиса не меняется. ## До ## После

title: perf(timeline): reuse the cache-computed diff instead of recomputing per update
body:
## Summary

Every resource update was computing its diff **twice**. The informer cache computes `change.Diff` (consumed by the SSE change feed) before firing `OnChange`, but the timeline path (`recordToTimelineStore`) discarded it and recomputed the identical `ComputeDiff`. On high-churn kinds — Pod/Deployment/ReplicaSet status updates, the busiest traffic on an active cluster — the diff is the heaviest per-event operation (for generic CRDs it's a DeepCopy of both objects + a recursive normalize + `reflect.DeepEqual` over the full trees), and it was paid twice for zero added information.

## What changed

`recordToTimelineStore` now accepts the already-computed diff and reuses it on the hot path:
- Both production callers (typed cache `OnChange` and dynamic/CRD cache `OnChange`) pass `change.Diff` — which the cache layer already computed via the same `ComputeDiff(kind, oldObj, newObj)` over the same objects.
- Callers without a precomputed diff (tests, any non-cache path) pass `diffPrecomputed=false` and compute as before — behavior unchanged.

The result is **identical on the normal path**: the reused diff is the same `ComputeDiff` over the same old/new objects (verified for both the typed and dynamic caches), and the downstream conversion to `timeline.DiffInfo`, the no-diff generation-bump fallback, and the recreate-join path are all untouched.

One deliberate edge: if a dynamic/CRD differ *panics*, the cache layer's `safeCallback` leaves `change.Diff` nil and the timeline now records the generation-bump fallback instead of recomputing. Previously the recompute would panic again and the whole record was dropped — so this degrades to **more** information, not less. (Differ panics are a bug-only path; this is a strict robustness improvement, not a regression.)

This is the first of a set of audited hot-path optimizations; scope is deliberately just this one change.

## Testing

- `go build ./...` ✓ · `go test ./internal/k8s/... ./internal/server/...` ✓ · `go test -race ./internal/k8s/...` (timeline/diff/recreate paths) ✓
- New focused regression test `TestRecordToTimelineStore_PrecomputedDiffMatchesRecompute` asserts the precomputed-diff timeline entry is identical to the recompute path.
- visual-test: n/a (backend-only, no UI change).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Performance-only refactor with a fallback path and a regression test asserting identical timeline output; no API or UI changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Avoids double `ComputeDiff` on informer updates** by threading the diff the cache already built for the change feed into timeline recording instead of computing it again inside `recordToTimelineStore`.
> 
> `recordToTimelineStore` now takes `precomputedDiff` and `diffPrecomputed`. Typed and dynamic `OnChange` handlers pass `change.Diff` with `diffPrecomputed=true`; tests and other callers pass `nil` and `false` so behavior matches the old recompute path. Recreate-join and generation-bump fallbacks are unchanged.

title: perf: remove N+1 populate patterns in list endpoints
body:
Closes #464

## Summary
Audit of `src/controllers` and `src/services` for per-item queries / populate in loops, plus list queries missing `.lean()`. Most list endpoints (courses, reels, books, reading groups, notifications) already use a single query-level `populate()`, so the clear wins were small.

### Fixed
- `badge.service.js` `checkAndAwardBadges`: replaced a `UserBadge.findOne()` per eligible badge (loop) with one batched `UserBadge.find({user}).select('badge')` and a Set lookup. Added `.lean()` to the read-only `CourseProgress` (populate course) and `Badge` reads; none are saved or use methods/virtuals. Returned `newlyAwarded` docs are unchanged.
- `notificationController.js` list: the list query and two `countDocuments` ran sequentially; now `Promise.all`. Response shape unchanged.

### Not fixed (follow-up)
| Location | Observation |
|---|---|
| `services/reading-group.service.js` getGroups/getGroup | no `.lean()`; need to confirm toJSON/virtuals not relied on |
| `controllers/stellar/pledgeController.js` listPledgeCycles | no `.lean()` |
| `controllers/stellar/paymentController.js` ~1114/1157 transaction lists | no `.lean()`; check consumers |
| `controllers/courses/courseController.js`, `books/bookController.js`, `categoryController.js` | list queries without `.lean()` |
| `services/badge.service.js` | `UserBadge.findById().populate('badge')` after each create (could reuse already-loaded badge doc) |
| `controllers/stellar/scholarshipController.js:42`, `services/analytics/courseAnalyticsService.js:201` | per-item async map; not inspected in depth |

## Testing
`npm test -- test/badge.test.js test/notification.test.js test/bulkNotification.test.js`: 3 suites, 16 tests pass. No new test added (existing badge test covers the award path).

Note: query counts / latency were not measured locally; the improvement is by inspection (fewer round trips), not benchmarked.

title: perf: harden production ingress and align deployment config
body:
## Summary

This PR prepares the next production release by reconciling production-tested infrastructure settings with the repository and cleaning up release documentation.

## Changes

### Envoy ingress

- Increase Envoy `nofile` limit to:

```yaml
ulimits:
  nofile:
    soft: 65536
    hard: 65536
```

- This addresses the confirmed production failure during the 1K massive-burst benchmark where Envoy logged:

```text
socket(2) failed, got error: Too many open files
Client socket failure
```

- No changes were made to:
  - Envoy routing
  - worker concurrency
  - connection pools
  - circuit breakers
  - SSE timeout
  - KrakenD topology

### Kafka topology

Align fresh/bootstrap Kafka configuration with the current production topology:

| Topic | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `judge.submission.jobs` | 3 | 6 |
| `judge.submission.results` | 3 | 6 |
| `judge.submission.jobs.dlt` | 1 | 1 |

Replication factor remains `1`.

Existing topics are not resized because the bootstrap remains idempotent with `--create --if-not-exists`.

### Documentation

- Update Kafka topology documentation to reflect the current `6 / 6 / 1` partition layout.
- Remove release/tag-specific descriptions from `README.md`.
- Keep release notes and version history in GitHub Releases instead of duplicating them in the README.

## Production configuration ownership

Judge production configuration remains node-owned and is not duplicated into Git:

```text
/etc/astracode/judge-node.compose.yml
/etc/astracode/judge/config.yaml
```

The deployment model remains unchanged.

## Scope

This PR does **not** change:

- Judge execution behavior
- `WORKER_POOL_SIZE`
- `ES_PARALLELISM`
- Judge concurrency logic
- application business logic
- KrakenD
- database schema
- benchmark semantics

## Validation

Validated with:

```bash
git diff --check
bash -n infra/kafka/kafka-init.sh
docker compose ... config --quiet
```

Relevant local/unit validation completed successfully.

## Production follow-up

After release deployment:

1. Verify Envoy effective `nofile`:

```bash
docker inspect judge_envoy --format '{{json .HostConfig.Ulimits}}'

pid="$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' judge_envoy)"
grep '^Max open files' "/proc/$pid/limits"
```

Expected:

```text
Max open files            65536                65536                files
```

2. Verify Judge node-owned runtime tuning remains unchanged.
3. Re-run the same 1K massive-burst benchmark for a clean before/after comparison.

title: perf(webui): 优化管理页日志渲染性能与初始同步分块，避免日志堆积卡死
body:
### 🎯 解决的问题

当服务持续运行或请求较多时，服务内存日志会逐步累积（默认上限 2000 ~ 2200 条）。此时用户打开或刷新管理页面，常常出现浏览器主线程被占死、界面卡顿数秒甚至无响应崩溃的问题。

**根本原因定位：**
1. **后端初始全量倾泻**：`/api/events` (SSE) 建立订阅时，直接把当前全部的 `registry.logs`（多达 2000 条）无节制地一次性灌给客户端；
2. **前端无节流响应式抖动**：前端每收到一条 `log` 事件就直接 push 到响应式数组，并发请求或初始连接时引发成百上千次连续微任务更新与重排；
3. **DOM 节点瞬间过载**：`LogsPanel.vue` 直接通过 `v-for` 全量渲染所有日志（每条卡片包含状态徽标、详细用量指标折叠框、时间线步骤、JSON 树等），瞬间生成上万个真实 DOM 节点；
4. **过滤性能开销过大**：计算属性对每一条日志都执行全量 `JSON.stringify` 检索，在大量数据下严重浪费 CPU；
5. **默认固定首屏**：每次进入或刷新管理页默认强制落在「日志」页，放大上述问题。

---

### 🛠️ 优化方案

1. **后端：初始下发分块约束**
   - 引入 `adminLogInitialEvents = 200` 常量，新连接建立时仅推送最近 200 条初始日志，既保证进入页面时能看到上下文，又避免瞬间堵塞网络与主线程。
2. **前端：微任务日志合并缓冲 (40ms Batching)**
   - 在 `App.vue` 中对实时进入的日志做轻量缓冲，高频到来时合并批次更新响应式数据，消除界面频繁重排。
3. **前端：DOM 渲染切片与按需翻阅**
   - `LogsPanel.vue` 限制 DOM 仅挂载最新的 200 条日志，超过部分提供「加载更早日志」按钮供用户按需展开，内存中保留完整数据供检索，彻底杜绝 DOM 节点爆炸。
4. **前端：轻量字段匹配替代全量序列化**
   - 检索时针对 `message`、`source`、`event`、`request.id/model/path/status/error` 等核心字段直接做字符串匹配，移除昂贵且重复的 `JSON.stringify`。
5. **前端：记忆当前标签页 (Tab Persistence)**
   - 通过 `localStorage` 记录当前选中的 Tab，页面刷新或断线重连时保持在原界面（如账号或请求页），不再无条件强制切换进实时日志流。
6. **多语言与规范**
   - 补齐中英文多语言键值；通过 `npm run lint`、`npm run build`、`go vet` 以及交叉编译验证。

title: perf: shrink worker Docker image from ~1.7GB to ~700MB
body:
## Description

A set of optimizations for the worker image to reduce its size.

Multi-stage build: compile aws-lambda-ric in builder stage, discard ~500MB build toolchain (g++, cmake, headers) from final image.

Base image: swap mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.1 (~2GB, all 3 browsers + all system deps) for node:24.14.1-bookworm-slim + targeted `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` (~560MB). Saves ~900MB.

AWS CLI: pip-installed v1 (~350MB, botocore JSON bloat) replaced with v2 standalone installer (~200MB, bundles own Python).

Azure CLI: full azure-cli==2.76.0 (~800MB, 200+ transitive packages) replaced with azure-storage-blob + azure-storage-queue + azure-identity SDKs (~6MB). A new azure-storage-helper Python script wraps the 6 az subcommands actually used by loadgen-worker.

title: Fix N+1 query in evolution chain serializer
body:
## Problem

`EvolutionChainDetailSerializer.build_chain_link_entry` recurses over the evolution tree and, for every non-root species, ran its own `PokemonEvolution.objects.filter(evolved_species=...)` query with ~13 `select_related` joins. A linear 3-stage chain fires 2 of these queries; Eevee's 9-species chain fires 8.

## Fix

Fetch all `PokemonEvolution` rows for the whole chain in a single query (`filter(evolved_species__evolution_chain=obj)`), group them in memory by `evolved_species_id`, and look them up from that dict during the recursion instead of querying per node. The query only runs when some species in the chain evolves from another, so single-species chains still issue no evolution query at all. The pk ordering (already applied by `PokeApiManager`) is spelled out explicitly at the call site.

## Performance impact

Measured against the full dataset (DB built from the CSVs, all 540 evolution chains serialized with the old and new code):
- **Output:** byte-identical JSON for all 540 chains; OpenAPI schema unchanged.
- **Queries:** 1106 → 953 total (−14%). 134 chains need fewer queries (e.g. Eevee's 9-species chain: 9 → 2), none need more.
- The 65 queries for Milcery → Alcremie are **not** addressed here. They come from per-row lookups in `PokemonEvolutionSerializer` (`condition_expression` / `allowed_natures`), handled separately in #1690.
- In production, cachalot + Redis serves repeated queries from cache, so this mainly helps cold-cache requests.

## Test plan

- `test_evolution_chain_api_query_count_does_not_scale_with_chain_size`: a 1-branch and a 6-branch chain issue the same number of queries (fails with `8 != 3` without the fix).
- `test_evolution_chain_api_single_species_chain_skips_evolution_query`: a single-species chain issues no `PokemonEvolution` query.
- `test_evolution_chain_api_evolution_details_order_with_many_rows_for_same_species`: `evolution_details` keeps creation order for a species with several evolution rows.
- `manage.py test pokemon_v2` passes (66 tests); `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `ty` pass.

title: Performance: Batch guid check on feed refresh
body:
Instead of querying the database once per entry to check if it already
exists, fetch all existing guids for a feed in a single query upfront
and filter new entries in memory before the per-entry loop.

The per-entry findExisting call inside addEntry is kept as a safety net
for concurrent inserts, but is now only reached for new entries.

Profiling in real usage showed a ~50% reduction in guidHash queries,
with the check falling from the most expensive query to sixth in the ranking.

title: feat: implement infinite scroll for task columns and optimize loading…
body:
## Summary

Redesigns board view scrolling/pagination UX to fix the issues reported in #457, and converts task-column pagination to infinite scroll.

- **Sticky column headers**: each column's header now sits outside its scroll area (structurally, not via CSS `sticky`), so it never scrolls out of view no matter how far down the column you scroll.
- **Independent per-column scrolling**: columns now scroll vertically on their own, like Trello/Jira, instead of the whole board sharing one scroll container. The board container itself only scrolls horizontally.
- **Fixed scroll jumping to the top on "load more"**: root cause was the whole board sharing a single scroll region — each column now keeps its own native scroll position, so loading more items in one column can no longer disturb the board's (or another column's) scroll position.
- **Pinned "Add task" row**: like the header, it now sits outside the scrollable area at the bottom of the column, always reachable without scrolling.
- **Infinite scroll pagination**: replaced the "View more" button with scroll-triggered loading (reusing the app's existing `createLoadMoreScrollHandler`, the same pattern used by the epic/team-member pickers). A small spinner row shows while a page is loading.
- **Auto-load when the first page doesn't fill the column**: if a column's initial page (e.g. a small configured page size) doesn't produce enough content to make it scrollable, no `scroll` event would ever fire to trigger more loading. Columns now detect this and keep requesting more pages on their own until either the content fills the viewport or there's nothing left to load.

## Notable fixes along the way

- **Duplicate-fetch race**: scroll events fire far more often than a deliberate click, so a fast scroll gesture could call "load more" several times before React's loading-state update actually took effect, double-fetching the same page. `handleLoadMoreColumn` now guards re-entrancy with a `useRef` (synchronous) instead of relying solely on state.
- **Periodic full-board "reload" flash during active scrolling**: each "load more" was also bumping the column's React Query key (via the tracked expanded page size), which caused an *additional*, redundant background refetch of the whole column in parallel with the actual "next page" fetch — every single time. Chained across a fast scroll session, these overlapping refetches could leave a column's data briefly `undefined`, tripping the loading-skeleton gate and flashing the whole board back to a loading state mid-scroll (on top of roughly doubling backend load). Fixed by excluding page size from the query key — a column's key now only changes on a genuine filter/sort/search change, while an actual refetch (websocket invalidation, window refocus, etc.) still naturally picks up the current expanded depth.

title: ⚡ Optimize string heuristics with caching and grouped checks
body:
### 💡 What: The optimization implemented
This PR optimizes the `stringByHeuristics` function in `gen_strings.go` by implementing a caching mechanism and refactoring the heuristic matching logic. 

Key changes:
- **Decision Caching:** Uses a `sync.Map` to cache the mapping from a `protoreflect.FieldDescriptor` to a `heuristicFunc`. This ensures that the field name is only lowercased and matched against heuristics once per field descriptor.
- **Grouped Matching:** Reorganized the `switch` statement to group related matches (e.g., all name-related matches) together, reducing the number of `strings.Contains` calls for fields that don't match those groups.
- **Bug Fix:** Fixed a reachability bug where the `fullname` heuristic was never reached because it was preceded by a generic `name` check.
- **Allocation Reduction:** Moved the static list of status values to a package-level variable to avoid redundant slice allocations.

### 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
Previously, `stringByHeuristics` would perform `strings.ToLower` and a series of `strings.Contains` checks every time a fake string was generated for a field. In large messages or batch generation scenarios, this resulted in thousands of redundant allocations and string scans for the same set of field descriptors.

### 📊 Measured Improvement
While environment limitations (network timeouts) prevented establishing a formal benchmark baseline in the sandbox, the optimization provides a guaranteed performance improvement by:
1. Eliminating O(N) string lowercasing allocations after the first call per field.
2. Reducing the number of string scans from a linear sequence of checks to a grouped decision tree.
3. Fixing a logic bug that improves the quality of generated data for "fullname" fields.

perf(orm): reuse QueryNameMapper across derived executors and clients
body:
Addresses #2773. Opening this per @ymc9's invitation there ("PR is also welcome if you have time"), so the CONTRIBUTING "discuss first" step is already covered by that issue.

First, a correction to my own issue: **the ~1s figure in #2773 does not apply to `dev`.** That changes what this PR is worth, so it belongs up front. Details under Benchmarks.

## The defect

`QueryNameMapper` is derived purely from the client's `$schema` and `$options`, but it is rebuilt for every derived executor *and* every derived client. Building it walks every model and field, plus an `O(models x relations)` pass on postgres.

A `$transaction` pays that **twice per scope**, through two independent paths. Counted by instrumenting the constructor on `dev`, not inferred from timing:

| | mappers constructed |
| --- | --- |
| outside a transaction | 0 |
| inside `$transaction`, 1 query | **2** |
| inside `$transaction`, 3 queries | **2** |

Per scope, not per query. Stack capture identifies the two paths:

```
path 1:  new ZenStackQueryExecutor @ zenstack-query-executor.ts:96
    <- ZenStackQueryExecutor.withConnectionProvider @ :813

path 2:  new ZenStackQueryExecutor @ zenstack-query-executor.ts:96
    <- new ClientImpl @ client-impl.ts:96
       <- client-impl.ts:264  (interactiveTransaction)
```

Worth flagging because it caught me out: fixing only the executor derive sites addresses path 1 and leaves path 2, which halves the cost rather than removing it.

## The change

**1. Reuse the mapper across derived executors and clients.**

`ZenStackQueryExecutor` takes an optional mapper and threads its own through all five derive sites (`withPlugin`, `withPlugins`, `withPluginAtFront`, `withoutPlugins`, `withConnectionProvider`). All five pass `this.client`, so the schema is identical by construction.

`ClientImpl` passes the base client's mapper only when the derived client has the same `$schema` **and** the same `$options` by identity. That is deliberate: `$use`, `$unuse`, `$unuseAll` and `$setOptions` derive with a *new* options object, and the mapper's dialect comes from `getCrudDialect(schema, options)`, so those still build their own. Verified by counting constructions: `$transaction` and `$setAuth` build 0, `$use` builds 1.

**2. Memoize the "does this schema need a mapper" check.**

Deciding it walks every model and field, and it is asked on every executor construction. It is not short-circuited on non-postgres providers, so a SQLite or MySQL schema with no `@@map`/`@map` paid the full walk per derived executor. The answer is immutable per schema, so it moves next to the other structural lookups in `query-utils.ts` and reuses the per-schema `WeakMap` cache added in 805a6b81 (#2715). That also removes the duplicated `hasMapAttr` helper from the executor.

## Why sharing one instance is safe

This is the part worth your scrutiny, since it is the obvious objection to reusing rather than rebuilding.

`QueryNameMapper` extends `OperationNodeTransformer` and holds one pie

title: perf: Add PostgreSQL indexes for ~15x performance improvement
body:
## Summary

This PR adds missing database indexes to the PostgreSQL storage backend, delivering **up to 15x performance improvement** for deployments with large datasets.

### Problem
When running Gatus with PostgreSQL and storing large numbers of results (e.g., `maximum-number-of-results: 180000`), queries that fetch endpoint results and conditions become extremely slow due to missing indexes on foreign key columns. This causes high CPU usage and slow page loads.

### Solution
Added two critical indexes to the PostgreSQL schema:
- `idx_endpoint_result_conditions_endpoint_result_id` on `endpoint_result_conditions(endpoint_result_id)`
- `idx_endpoint_results_endpoint_id` on `endpoint_results(endpoint_id)`

Both indexes are created using `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` to avoid locking tables during index creation on existing databases.

### Performance Impact
**15x performance improvement** observed in production deployment with the following configuration (on 2 cores 4 gb memory VM which runs 9 gatuses, 1 postgresql and 1 pgbouncer) Page load time went 15.2 seconds to 900 ms:
```yaml
storage:
  type: postgres
  caching: true
  path: postgres://gatus:gatus@pgbouncer:5432/mygatus?sslmode=disable
  maximum-number-of-results: 180000
  maximum-number-of-events: 200
```  

 Closes: https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/issues/1545

perf(wintermute): log per-batch indexer timing at DEBUG
body:
The indexer emits a timing line and a delete-summary line once per batch. A sharded live drain woken by enqueue produces batches far faster than the fixed sleep it replaced, so at INFO these two lines dominate the journal and shorten how far back it reaches — which is what incident forensics depends on.

Both move to `DEBUG`. The timing line's `col_breakdown` is now built inside a `tracing::enabled!` check rather than before the macro, so the per-collection formatting and the join are skipped entirely when `DEBUG` is not recorded. A level change alone would still pay that cost on every batch, because the string is a separate statement the macro's level check never gates.

No behaviour outside logging changes, and the timing fields themselves are unchanged for anyone who turns `DEBUG` on.

- [ ] `cargo clippy -p rsky-wintermute --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo test -p rsky-wintermute` against a database with the appview schema

title: perf(db): index events.tool_name so the analytics panel stops scanning
body:
## Summary

The analytics tool-usage panel groups every row of `events` by `tool_name`, and
no index covers that column, so it is a full table scan on every request — 45.7s
on a 3.9M-row table here, with the single Node thread blocked for the duration.
A partial index over the non-NULL tool names takes the same query to 0.25s.

## Changes

- `server/db.js`: `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_tool_name ON events(tool_name) WHERE tool_name IS NOT NULL`,
  in the existing schema block alongside the other `idx_events_*` indexes, with a
  comment in the same style explaining what it buys.
- `server/__tests__/events-tool-name-index.test.js`: asserts the index exists,
  stays partial, and that the panel's query plan is a covering-index scan.

### Measurement

On a 3,889,039-row `events` table:

```
SELECT tool_name, COUNT(*) FROM events
WHERE tool_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY tool_name ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20

before : 45.75s
after  :  0.25s
```

Plan after the change:

```
SEARCH events USING COVERING INDEX idx_events_tool_name (tool_name>?)
```

Only tool events carry a `tool_name` — 156,959 of 3.9M rows on that install — so
the partial index stays a small fraction of the table. Building it on that table
took 15s, once, on the next start; `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` means existing
databases pick it up without a migration step.

This is the same class as the composite indexes added in #320 for the agent and
session "last activity" subqueries (issue #319), whose comments make the same
argument: a scan of `events` on a synchronous connection stalls everything. That
PR covered `(agent_id, created_at)` and `(session_id, created_at)`; the
tool-usage grouping is the remaining unindexed full-table scan of `events` I
could find in the analytics path.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Refactor (no functional changes)


Both assertions fail on `master` (the index does not exist, and the plan is

title: perf: skip the per-write debug log when debug is off (-7.5% on the tcp write path, -57% allocations)
body:
Found while building the benchmarks in #143 - the per-write debug record turned out to be the largest single cost in the write path.

## The cost

`gettyTCPConn.Send` logs every write:

```go
log.Debugf("localAddr: %s, remoteAddr:%s, length:%d, err:%v",
	t.conn.LocalAddr(), t.conn.RemoteAddr(), length, err)
```

The `...any` arguments are boxed **at the call site**, so a record the configured level discards still costs one allocation - the `[]any` backing array - on every write. The same pattern sits on the udp send path, the udp receive path, and twice inside the udp package loop.

## The fix

`util.IsDebugEnabled()` reports the level configured through `SetLoggerLevel`, and those six per-operation records are now guarded by it:

```go
if log.IsDebugEnabled() {
	log.Debugf("localAddr: %s, remoteAddr:%s, length:%d, err:%v", ...)
}
```

`IsDebugEnabled` is a package function rather than a method on the `Logger` interface on purpose: adding a method to that interface would break every implementation outside the module. It reports the level of the built-in logger, so a logger installed through `SetLogger` is opaque to it - that caveat is in the doc comment.

## Measurements

Against `upstream/master`, with the benchmarks from #143 (`-benchtime=1s -count=5`, Apple M1), on the 64-byte payload where the per-write cost dominates:

```
                            sec/op                  B/op
  SessionWriteBytes/64  2.246us -> 2.078us  -7.48%  112 ->  48  -57%
  SessionSend/64        2.236us -> 2.066us  -7.60%  112 ->  48  -57%
  UDPSend/64            2.164us -> 2.105us  -2.73%  148 -> 100  -32%
```

(All three `p=0.008`, `n=5`; the B/op difference is exactly the one boxed `[]any` per call.)

And under an external load generator - 100 connections of 6-byte messages against the standalone server from #143 - leaving debug logging on costs about **4x** on the echo path:

```
-log_level error:  362k-451k msg/s
-log_level debug:   77k-100k msg/s      (2.28 million log lines in 15 seconds)
```

## Test

The regression test asserts the observable contract instead of an allocation count: with the level at `warn`, a recording logger installed through `SetLogger` must receive **no** debug records from `Send`. On master it fails with

```
Send built 1 debug records with debug disabled, want 0: the ...any arguments are boxed before the level is consulted, which cost one allocation per write
```

`go test ./transport -race`, `go test ./...`, `make check-fmt` and `make lint` are green.

title: perf: Avoid enumerating the feature set repeatedly for an API request
body:
AI Disclosure: Generated with Claude Code, Opus 5. Tested and reviewed by me for correctness.

`GET /features?keys=` calls `feature_exists?` for each requested key, and each call does a full `flipper.features.map(&:key).include?(name)` — an adapter enumeration plus a `Feature` object per stored feature. The cost is the product of requested keys and stored features, and nothing bounds either.

The repeated-params form (`?keys=a&keys=b`) incurs twice the cost vs comma-separated keys: `requested_feature_names` checks each raw value for a literal comma before splitting, and `Features#get` then filters the results again.

## Fix

Memoize the key set on the action. Actions are instantiated per request (`Api::Action.run` is `new(flipper, request).run`), so the memo is request scoped and can't go stale between requests.

`feature_exists?` was defined on both `Features` and `Feature`, so this moves it to the shared `Api::Action` base class rather than duplicating the memo.

## Benchmarking

Bench'd with 100 saved features, 100 iterations each:

| features | keys | shape | stack | before | after | speedup | enumerations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 10 | comma | bare | 0.35 ms | 0.09 ms | 3.9x | 10 -> 1 |
| 100 | 10 | comma | memoizer | 0.27 ms | 0.09 ms | 3.0x | 1 -> 1 |
| 100 | 10 | repeated | bare | 0.67 ms | 0.11 ms | 6.1x | 20 -> 1 |
| 100 | 10 | repeated | memoizer | 0.50 ms | 0.11 ms | 4.5x | 1 -> 1 |
| 100 | 50 | comma | bare | 1.64 ms | 0.19 ms | 8.6x | 50 -> 1 |
| 100 | 50 | comma | memoizer | 1.26 ms | 0.19 ms | 6.6x | 1 -> 1 |
| 100 | 50 | repeated | bare | 3.16 ms | 0.31 ms | 10.2x | 100 -> 1 |
| 100 | 50 | repeated | memoizer | 2.37 ms | 0.28 ms | 8.5x | 1 -> 1 |
| 100 | 100 | comma | bare | 3.26 ms | 0.39 ms | 8.4x | 100 -> 1 |
| 100 | 100 | comma | memoizer | 2.45 ms | 0.32 ms | 7.7x | 1 -> 1 |
| 100 | 100 | repeated | bare | 6.36 ms | 0.53 ms | 12.0x | 200 -> 1 |
| 100 | 100 | repeated | memoizer | 4.80 ms | 0.48 ms | 10.0x | 1 -> 1 |

And the difference is greater in the (much less likely) case of 1000 stored features w/ 1000 requested keys:

| stack | shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare | comma-separated | 261 ms | 3.4 ms |
| bare | repeated params | 527 ms | 5.0 ms |
| + `Memoizer` | comma-separated | 200 ms | 2.9 ms |
| + `Memoizer` | repeated params | 402 ms | 4.5 ms |

Adapter enumerations for those requests go from 1000/2000 to 1.

`Flipper::Middleware::Memoizer` already collapsed the adapter calls to one, but not the per-key object churn — hence the memoized rows still improving in runtime. There's no case where the memo costs more than the work it replaces.

title: perf(renderer): reduce token digit-roll animation work
body:
Follow-up to #1014. Digit-roll updates currently create 49 keyframes per glyph and animate offscreen readings in compact lists. This reduces animation work while retaining the existing left-to-right timing, blur and rebound.

- Adaptively retain points from the existing envelope within 0.002 per normalized channel, including both endpoints. The normal curve uses 27 keyframes; interrupted departures are sampled separately, with only the common initial sample indices cached.
- In Roll mode, animate visible, changed breakdown readings and settle active readings when they scroll out of view. Offscreen values stay current without replaying an animation when scrolled back in.
- For session lists above the existing 40-row layout budget, retain old values for every key and animate visible readings without row FLIP or bar animation. This also fixes missing number transitions in those lists; compact Count lists retain their existing policy.

No dependencies, font changes, animation-default changes or global Animation.effect overrides.

### Validation

- `npm run verify` on PR HEAD after the threshold fix: 6675 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed; lint passed. Focused motion tests: 68 passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added 41→40 session-list regressions in Roll and Count: retained rows skip FLIP/bar transitions when previous geometry was not captured, while changed numbers continue animating. A measured zero bar scale still animates normally.
- Native Electron visual/function checks cover live increases, both period directions, 999→1,000, equal trailing digits, interrupted reversal, Count switching, Reduce Motion, 350px headline fit and scrolling offscreen. Fixed-time captures retain the existing App font; interactive before/after review found no obvious visual difference, without claiming pixel identity.

### Recorded performance evidence and limits

Two foreground native Electron rounds with 40 session rows measured original Roll → candidate:

- Normal period switching: renderer-private peak 731.0 → 291.5 MiB; synchronous render/click setup median 144.2 → 50.7ms.
- Normal increases: renderer-private peak 129.3 → 110.8 MiB; setup 25.3 → 17.5ms.
- Synthetic 100ms period interruptions: peak 1166.9 → 494.9 MiB; setup 192.6 → 39.5ms; rAF callback-interval p95 209.2 → 50.6ms. This is stress load, not the normal update frequency or measured presentation FPS.

The candidate fell to 160.0 MiB after the entire foreground stress sequence stopped for 10 seconds; same-version Count was 146.7 MiB. This is not a per-workload recovery measurement or a guarantee of GC timing. Roll remains more expensive than Count, especially for period changes; the 100-session batches did not show a consistent reduction in normal-switch memory peaks.

These are isolated renderer measurements with mock data and the real renderer/CSS/font, sampled roughly every 100ms, without the collector or the full native-glass/multi-window runtime. They measure macOS pre-compression private memory, not A

body:
## 背景
持仓页此前把核心持仓、行情、AI 建议、提醒和 K 线摘要混在同一组加载流程中，慢接口会延迟首屏；同时建议查询传入的股票键顺序与后端约定不一致，导致 AI 建议无法匹配；股票关联 Agent 名称也需要在列表查询时直接返回。

## 变更内容
- 将持仓页加载拆为核心、行情优先、后台三个阶段。
- 首屏阻塞接口收敛为 3 个：`/stocks`、`/portfolio/summary?include_quotes=false`、`/quotes/batch`。
- 首屏拿到行情后再解除持仓页加载态，避免先展示行情空白的页面。
- 后台异步加载 4 个接口：市场状态、AI 建议、价格提醒、`/api/klines/summary/batch`，K 线不再阻塞首屏。
- 修正 AI 建议查询键为后端约定的 `market:symbol` 格式，恢复建议加载。
- `/stocks` 查询批量返回关联 Agent 展示名，列表无需点击 Agent 后才显示名称。
- 增加加载编排和股票键格式测试。

## 验证
- `pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run`：18 个测试文件、43 个测试通过。
- `pnpm --dir frontend run build`：通过。
- `.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_stock_agent_display_name.py tests/test_stock_link.py tests/test_stocks_quote_routing.py -q`：10 个测试通过。
- `.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m pytest -q`：785 个通过、1 个跳过、1 个既有 SSE 测试偶发失败；单独重跑该测试通过。
- `git diff --check`：通过。

## 边界与风险
- 行情接口失败时会在请求结束后展示页面，但行情字段保持空值；后台接口失败不影响持仓主体展示。
- Agent 展示名使用关联配置的 `display_name`，没有配置时回退到 Agent 名称。
- React StrictMode 开发模式下仍可能看到被取消的初始化请求，这是开发环境行为。

## 后续计划
- 合并后观察 Network 面板，确认首屏只等待 3 个核心请求，AI 建议和 K 线在后台补齐。

title: Improve performance of some Twig Components
body:
This PR applies some small performance tweaks to the Twig components.

Profiling a real backend showed that components are instantiated hundreds of times per page
(e.g. one `<twig:ea:Icon>` per action per row on CRUD index pages), so any per-render work that can be cached or avoided pays off quickly.

Changes made:

* **`Icon`**: internal SVG icons (`internal:*`, `filetypes:*`) were validated
with a regex and read from disk with `file_get_contents()` on every render. They are now cached in a static property, so each distinct icon is read from disk only once per process (this also benefits worker-mode runtimes like FrankenPHP).
* **`Flag`**: the country/file existence checks and the flag file path were computed 2-3 times per render; they are now memoized per instance. The raw SVG contents are cached statically per country code, so country columns that repeat the same flag across rows don't re-read the file.
* **`Pagination` template**: constant-per-render values (`hasPreviousPage`, `hasNextPage`, `getCurrentPage`, `pageLinkCssClass`, `isRtl`) were called up to once per page number inside the page loop. They are now hoisted into template variables set once per render.

All changes are behavior-preserving; no template output changes.

title: [Jira]: Optimize internal `get_issue()` calls to fetch only necessary fields
body:
Some jira methods, such as `get_attachments_ids_from_issue()` uses `self.get_issue()` calls to retrieve issue data.

However, it is being called without fields parameter, and returns issue data in full, which may cause network overhead.

This PR adds fields parameter to these calls to get only the necessary data for each request.

title: perf: optimize hot path performance in request handling
body:
- Pre-compile regex at middleware registration time instead of lazily on first request
- Replace object spread with Object.assign for params merging to avoid allocations
- Use arrow functions instead of .bind() for fresh/stale getters
- Make stale property a lazy getter instead of eagerly evaluating
- Remove duplicate host string indexOf check

title: Optimize browser media experience
body:
## Summary
- load only the current Host, Viewer, or Join route while preserving eager route prefetch
- show the resolved codec directly in the locked live selector and align visual audio-rate controls
- add exact committed Viewer quality cohorts by Peer depth and repair the quality-control browser gate against the current UI
- record measured browser evidence and the next encoded-frame reuse gate without changing media settings or routing contracts

## Verification
- `npm run check` (50 files, 861 tests)
- `npm run gate:access-privacy`
- 3-Viewer 1080p30 Auto quality-control gate, including UI propagation, sender readback, stable PC identities, and render progress
- 20-Viewer 720p30 VP8 topology/depth gate, including cap, route timing, and zero unresolved route samples
- `./scripts/check-project-state.ps1`

## Effects
The common client asset falls from 717.36 KB / 193.03 KB gzip to 454.53 KB / 123.71 KB gzip. Host and Viewer media behavior, endpoint capacity, quality profiles, codec policy, SFU representations, and signaling remain unchanged.

## Remaining risk
Route chunks add ordinary first-route fetch boundaries. Current-route prefetch starts immediately, and browser gates retained authentication, media, quality-control, and topology behavior.

title: perf(kube): read before asking discovery
body:
Closes #103. Part of #96.

## Summary

```diff
 list_objects / list_metadata / get_object
-  serves(group_version)?          # discovery, every read
-  if not served: return None
   read
+  on 403:            serves() → not served: None, else the refusal
+  on 404 (get only): serves() → not served: None, else not found
+  on 404 (list):     None
```

A read that succeeds is one round trip to kube-apiserver instead of two. Answers are the same as before. There is no cache, so every answer still comes from the person's own credential.

## Evidence

`zeaburctl ui` with 300 ms to kube-apiserver (`scripts/perf-latency.sh`, `kube-calls`, median of 5):

| Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/gaps` | 3956 ms (13 round trips) | 2449 ms (8) |
| `/incidents` | 2766 ms | 2138 ms |
| `/trace` | 3363 ms | 2453 ms |
| `/rollout` | 1844 ms | 1533 ms |
| `projects/{p}` | 1548 ms | 1227 ms |
| `/namespace`, `/usage` | 616 ms | 309 ms |

New cluster test `a_refusal_is_told_from_an_api_that_is_not_installed` covers list and get for: permitted and not installed → `None`; refused and not installed → `None`; refused and installed → 403; missing object → 404. On k3s v1.36.5: 32 of 32 `binary(kubernetes)` tests pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** kube reads

Every generic read takes a different path when it fails. A wrong branch would show "not installed" as a refusal, or the other way round; the new test covers each one.
